Overview

Home of the Cobalt Reserve, Tal'Dorei's greatest library and archive, of Westhall Academy and, in its shadow, of the College of the Savvy, the arts school founded by the bard known as the White Duke. The air smells of old parchment and fresh ink.

Tal'Dorei's greatest house of knowledge: anything can be researched here — but nothing leaves without the Cobalt Soul knowing.
{{local:college-savvy}} Arts schoolSafe
Theater, music and poetry at all hours, under the mask of the mysterious White Duke.
{{local:greystone-tower}} Archmage's towerHigh
The Realmseer's tower, wrapped in a storm that never leaves — something inside wants out.
{{local:ljunian}} School for magically gifted youthsLow
A scorched-walled house where children with wild magic learn not to blow things up.
{{local:westhall-academy}} Academy of arts and sciencesSafe
A proud school open to any talent from the plains — good for finding a specialist, a map or an argument.

A tower too tall for its neighborhood, where the Scions of Yuminor read the stars — and sell a little luck.

The most important gods of the Dividing Plains are the Lawbearer, the Wildmother and the Platinum Dragon, and their sanctuaries show it: the First Bastion, the Wild Arbor and the Platinum Dragon's Rest. Overview

A small ward packed with great temples to the Prime Deities. The most important gods of the Dividing Plains are the Lawbearer, the Wildmother and the Platinum Dragon, and their sanctuaries show it: the First Bastion, the Wild Arbor and the Platinum Dragon's Rest. Freedom of worship is guaranteed here.

{{local:first-bastion}} Great temple of the LawbearerSafe
The ward's most imposing temple: marble and worn gold, a memory of when it hid refugees during the occupation.
{{local:templo-onimartelo}} Forge-temple of the All-HammerSafe
A dark stone hall with a sacred forge unlit never since the rebuilding: every hammer stroke is a prayer.
{{local:raven-shrine}} Shrine of the Matron of RavensSafe
A dark shrine in an alley, where the dead are recorded and no one is allowed to come back wrong.
{{local:santuario-tecela}} Shrine of the Moon WeaverSafe
A small silver shrine, visited at night, where people pray for peaceful sleep and keep secrets.
{{local:temple-terrace}} Avenue of templesSafe
An esplanade of temples and no stalls: bells of many gods ringing at different hours and pilgrims of every faith.
{{local:templo-comutadora}} Rotunda of the ChangebringerSafe
A noisy temple of the goddess of change and freedom: open assemblies and help for those arriving with nothing.
{{local:templo-alvorecer}} Temple of the DawnfatherSafe
A golden roof and a sun disc that blazes at dawn: the plains' god of harvests, with an infirmary for those who cannot pay.
{{local:templo-tempestade}} Temple of the Storm LordLow
A temple of courage and fair battle with a sand arena in front: duels every afternoon and Shields praying before patrol.
{{local:platinum-rest}} Temple of the Platinum DragonSafe
A serene temple of alabaster and silver that shelters the forgotten and the hungry; home of the paladin Lady Kima of Vord.
{{local:wild-arbor}} Tree-temple of the WildmotherSafe
A gigantic living tree with chambers in its trunk — the Wildmother's temple, where nothing is pruned.

Overview

The central district and municipal heart of the city. It has no housing: here stand the Lord Mayor's Residence, the Hall of Reason and the public square with the Black King.

{{local:barkley-manor}} Wealthy family manorLow
Cattle-and-wagon wealth on display a few blocks from the tenements — and a youngest son drowning in debt.
{{local:clasp-manhole}} Secret Underwalk entranceModerate
An ordinary manhole bearing the city crest — and the Clasp's front door for those who know the knock.
{{local:hall-of-reason}} Courthouse and squareSafe
The city courthouse, elven in style, with the Platinum Dragon in flight above the door and the founder's fountain in the square.
{{local:ironhand}} Construction-materials warehouseLow
The company that rebuilt half the city after the war: no one likes it, no one builds anything big without it.
{{local:lord-mayor}} Seat of government and barracksSafe
From here the Lord Mayor rules Westruun, shares power with an indebted council and dispatches the Shields of the Plain.
{{local:public-forum}} Civic square and guardian statueSafe
The heart of the Opal Ward, where proclamations are read, protests gather and festivals spill over — watched by the Black King, the statue that wakes.
{{local:trickfoot-park}} Public parkLow
The Opal Ward's green breath: shade, a pond, a bandstand — and no one paying attention to anyone.

It is also rife with crime: the Clasp and the Myriad feed on the tension between the poor and the rich living a block apart. Freedom of worship is not guaranteed here, even at home.

Where most of the city lives: narrow streets, taverns, bakeries and the stair down to the Underwalk.

Overview

The most crowded ward, home to two thirds of the population. It has no great landmarks, but every neighborhood has its own culture — beloved bakeries, shops and pubs. It is also rife with crime: the Clasp and the Myriad feed on the tension between the poor and the rich living a block apart. Freedom of worship is not guaranteed here, even at home.

{{local:casa-luz-eterna}} Small temple (the Everlight)Safe
A humble temple for seeking forgiveness; neutral ground where neither Shields nor Clasp arrest anyone.
{{local:sewer-entrance}} Sewer entranceModerate
An iron grate in an alley leading to the old sewers — giant rats, smugglers and unmapped passages.
{{local:softsky}} Family bakerySafe
A tiny, nearly broke bakery with the best smell on the street; Elowen and her son Simon do everything themselves.
{{local:sunkissed}} Tavern and innLow
An honest tavern for farmers and travelers, with a vine-covered yard, a stable and rooms upstairs; the half-orc Ulf behind the bar knows everything happening in the ward. The cellar is larger than it should be.
{{local:vaca-de-sela}} Tavern (Clasp front)Moderate
The loudest tavern in the city: music, gambling and cheap ale — and, behind the service door, the Clasp's hideout.
{{local:underwalk-gates}} Main entrance to the UnderwalkModerate
A forty-foot-wide staircase descending from the Residential Ward into the ward beneath the city — and the easiest adventuring work to find.
{{local:velvet-kettle}} TeahouseSafe
Spiced tea and gossip at the same speed; the owner trades a secret for a secret, never for coin.

Most of the city's businesses, stalls and warehouses, many rebuilt by the League of Miracles. A patched tent outside, huge inside; the gnome owner talks to his wares and knows too much about whoever walks in.
{{local:exandrian-exchange}} Auction houseLow
Polished marble and gilded grilles: auctions of antique weapons, jewels and artifacts of uncertain origin, with League of Miracles money behind them.

The colorful branch of Tal'Dorei's most famous shop: glowing windows, high prices and charming service.
{{local:dream-stall}} Dream-reading stallSafe
The purple stall of tiefling twins Nyx and Vryll, packed since the nightmares began — guilty, or just opportunists?
{{local:red-house}} Family home (safe house)Safe
The red-brick house of the large Trickfoot family: always a pot on the fire and shelter for anyone in trouble.
{{local:sakenar}} Street fairLow
A noisy fair filling a whole square: food, cloth, spices — and goods of doubtful origin after noon.

Packed floor to ceiling, no questions about where anything came from — and almost always something valuable buried in it.

Interior scenes{{cenas:cobalt-reserve}}

Read aloud

Inside, the silence has weight. Rows of polished stone shelves climb past the reach of the floating lanterns, linked by spiral stairs and thin metal walkways. Every sound — a scroll unrolled, a sandal on marble — echoes longer than it should. A single shaft of daylight cuts the atrium on the diagonal. A monk in cobalt robes approaches without hurry, hands hidden in her sleeves: "What are you looking for — and why?"

Senses

Sight

A blue stone dome, columns carved with the open eye, stone shelves vanishing upward, floating lanterns.

Sound

Heavy silence; pages turning; sandals on marble; a low bell marks each hour.

Smell

Old parchment, beeswax and iron-gall ink.

Who is here

{{npc:greisalda}}
High Curator of the Cobalt Reserve, keeper of the Cobalt Soul's secrets
“I remember everything. Including what you'd rather I forgot.”
{{ficha:greisalda}}
{{npc:cressida}}
Expositor (field agent) of the Cobalt Soul
“Smile. You're being watched — by me.”
{{ficha:cressida}}
{{npc:salomane}}
Archivist who (reluctantly) helps adventurers research
“No, it's not in the catalogue. Yes, I looked. Twice.”
{{ficha:salomane}}

Services and prices

ServicePrice
Research in the public stacks (1 hour, escorted)free; a 1 gp donation is appreciated
A scribe copies a document2 gp per page
Consult a specialist monk (genealogy, history, heraldry)5 gp
Access to a restricted archivea favor to the order, never coin

Rules

Research. One hour in the public stacks allows an Intelligence (History) DC 15 check to learn any piece of common knowledge about Tal'Dorei; on a failure, try again after another hour. Sensitive lore sits in the restricted archives, open only to Cobalt Soul members or those in the order's good graces.

Escort. Every visitor is assigned a monk who is both guide and watchman.

Secret (GM only)

The Cobalt Soul does not keep books purely for love of learning: it watches over dangerous secrets and uses them to keep power in Tal'Dorei balanced. The monks log what every visitor researches — and that log has sent more than one conspirator to prison.

Adventure hooks

The missing pageLow level · 1–4

A volume of the Occupation Register came back to its shelf with a page torn out. The curator wants to know who took it, quietly — and pays in access to the restricted archives.

The reader who never leavesMid level · 5–10

A scholar has sat at the same desk for nine days, not eating, copying the same book. The monks cannot move him — and the book was never in the catalogue.

Rumors (roll 1d6)

1The monks fight as well as they read — better not steal anything.True
2There are floors below the dome never opened to the public.True
3The curator owns a book that tells the reader's future.False
4The order pays well for old manuscripts found in the Underwalk.True
5The monks never sleep: they take turns with magical copies of themselves.False
6Someone inside the order is selling information to the League of Miracles.True

Groups argue in the courtyard with such conviction they seem about to come to blows — until everyone laughs a second later. Above them the oxidized copper dome glows low in the afternoon sun.

Sight

Sand-colored stone, a green copper dome, open arched windows, banners without crests.

Sound

Heated debates in the courtyard, a class bell, laughter, someone reciting formulas.

Smell

Chalk, ink, trimmed grass and bread brought from home.

Who is here

{{npc:estella}}

“Talent is common. Discipline is rare. Which did you bring?”

Services and prices

ServicePrice

Rules

The lord mayor does her best to let any promising student from the plains attend free of charge: mages, architects, poets, artists and agriculturalists.

Secret (GM only)

A group of students meets at night in the chemistry cellar trying to recreate Umbrasyl's acid “to study the cure”. They have already lost a finger and gained a mysterious patron.

Adventure hooks

Final examLow level · 1–4

The engineering class must test a rope bridge at the edge of the Bramblewood and wants an escort. Something in the forest likes rope.

Rumors (roll 1d6)

1The headmistress descends from a famous wizard and dislikes talking about it.True
2Those who cannot pay study for free — the mayor insists on it.True
3The copper dome is a lightning rod feeding Greystone Tower.False
4The Academy and the Ljunian School fight over the best talents.True
5A student turned into a frog and no one noticed for a semester.False
6An anonymous patron is paying for night experiments in the cellar.True

Rules

Star reading (10 gp, once per day). The Scions of Yuminor read the sky for a character: roll a d20 and note it. Within the next 24 hours, that result can replace any d20 rolled by a creature the character can see.

Headmistress Estella Ladimar, a descendant of the wizard Atz Yuminor, supports the order. The diviners are friendly, yet something about them is off — as if they stared at the stars a little too long.

Secret (GM only)

The oldest diviners saw something in the stars that none of them discuss. Since then they chalk an X on a calendar date — and move it whenever that date draws near.

Adventure hooks

The fallen starMid level · 5–10

A “star” fell on the plains to the north and the diviners want the fragment before the Ravagers find it. It is warm, it pulses — and it has an owner.

Rumors (roll 1d6)

1The star reading really works: whoever pays gets a lucky day.True
2The diviners always seem a little absent, like people who stared at the sky too long.True
3From the top you can see Emon on a clear night.False
4They avoid talking about a certain date.True
5The whole tower rotates once a year.False
6The headmistress uses the observatory to spy on Greystone Tower.False

locais.narracao: The tower simply looks wrong. As you watch, green smoke escapes from a crack in the stone and vanishes far too fast to be natural.
locais.ganchos: An Assistant's Plight (mid level). Inside, the halls shift as if the tower were thinking. Challenge after challenge, the party learns that Ryndarien is trying to keep something far more dangerous imprisoned.

Sound

Who is here

{{npc:eskil}}
Realmseer, archmage of Greystone Tower

The Realmseer's assistant

Secret (GM only)

The archmage is not trapped by accident: he locked himself in on purpose to keep something contained. If the party “rescues” him the wrong way, they release what he is holding.

Adventure hooks

An Assistant's PlightMid levelOfficial hook

The party receives a letter from Jekt, assistant to Realmseer Eskil Ryndarien: the archmage vanished inside his own tower, which now keeps everyone out — and him in. Inside, the halls shift as if the tower were thinking. Challenge after challenge, the party learns that Ryndarien is trying to keep something far more dangerous imprisoned.

Talking stonesLow level · 1–4

Pebbles from the tower turn up in city gutters and whisper at night. Jekt pays to collect them all before someone learns what they say.

Rumors (roll 1d6)

1The rain falls only on the tower — the rest of the street stays dry.True
2The archmage's assistant is desperate and seeking adventurers.True

An arts school founded by the bard known as the White Duke, in the shadow of Westhall Academy. Music, theater and poetry spill from its windows at all hours.

The building is an old auction house turned inside out: the main hall became a theater, the storerooms became rehearsal rooms, and the attic holds a hoard of sheet music and costumes nobody dares to catalogue. Tuition is free for anyone who passes the audition — and auditions are public, on the front steps, the first morning of every month.

A small school for youngsters with uncommon gifts — magic that woke too early and needs a firm hand.

It occupies a three-story house with reinforced windows and walls scorched on the inside. The teachers are few, patient and seasoned: they teach control before they teach spells. Many families from the plains villages send children here who began making strange things happen by accident.

locais.descricao:
The city's great square, heart of the Opal Ward, where announcements are read, protests gather and festivals spill over. At its center stands the Black King: a dark statue of Palest Westruun on a rearing horse.

The forum is the civic heart of the city: proclamations are read here, major trials draw crowds, and any citizen may climb the low step at the statue's foot to speak. The statue of Palest on horseback is dark, smooth and enormous; children dare each other to touch the horse's hoof.
locais.narracao: Decades in the open have left a dull patina on the stone and lichen in the folds of the carved cloak. A pair of pigeons rests calmly on the statue's shoulder — as if they knew, in some animal way, that it is no danger. For now.

It was blessed by the high priest of the First Bastion. When the safety of the whole city is threatened it awakens: a stone golem with 60 ft. speed, Intelligence and Charisma 18 (+4), speaking Common. Dour, regal and single-minded about protecting its people. (Sheet: actor The Black King.)

The Black King wakes only when the whole city is in danger — but someone has found a way to fool it into waking against a single target.

At dawn the Black King's horse faces a different way. No one saw anything. The whole city wants to know what it is watching.

A tree-lined park in the heart of the Opal Ward, a rare green breath among public buildings. Shaded benches, a small pond and townsfolk lunching on the grass.

The park is named for a halfling family of the Residential Ward that helped the city during the occupation. There is a bandstand where students of the College of the Savvy play for free, a little pond with bad-tempered ducks, and a bronze plaque honoring those who fought in the streets when the dragons came.

The Underwalk. The city's newest ward lies beneath it: sewers, military bunkers and the wine cellars of destroyed mansions, dug in haste during the Chroma Conclave's invasion. It sat abandoned for over twenty years, save for the very poor. In the past two years entrepreneurs have tried to turn it into a living neighborhood — and they hire adventurers by the dozen, because every day brings a new rumor of many-headed things in the tunnels.

locais.narracao: Something glows faintly among the branches — fireflies, or perhaps not.

locais.descricao:
A quiet shrine to the Matron of Ravens, of dark stone and black candles, where families leave feathers and coins for their dead.

The shrine sits in a narrow alley, far from the splendor of the Temple Terrace — the Matron of Ravens asks for no display. A veiled priestess receives the bereaved, records the dead in a thick ledger and makes sure no one comes back as they shouldn't.
locais.narracao: Dozens of black candles burn without smoke. Raven feathers are tucked into every crack of the stone. A real raven watches you from atop the altar, unblinking.

locais.descricao:
An upscale inn of stained-glass windows and a liveried doorman, for wealthy merchants and passing nobles. A room here costs what many earn in a month.

Rooms have a bathtub, a private fireplace and linen sheets from Emon. In the hall below, merchants close deals over expensive wine, and the manager — an elf who never forgets a debt — keeps a list of who is welcome and who is not.
locais.narracao: The doorman looks you over from boots to hat before opening the door. Inside, light through the stained glass paints the floor amber and red. Nobody speaks loudly here.

imagens.leg: Amber and red light falls from the stained glass onto the waxed floor. A doorman in livery measures everyone who enters. Merchants and nobles dine in low voices among polished wood and brass, and standing, unhurried, an elf in a dark coat watches the whole room.

Two-colored marble, a medallion with the chalice set in the floor and, at the back, the imperial staircase rising in three flights of wine-red runner. To the right, the front desk; to the left, the weapon check. At the foot of the stairs two golden statues hold torches, and no one has ever seen them lit.

The hall is the noisy heart of the house, and even it speaks softly. Round tables with cloths to the floor, silver, flowers, a candle inside an amber goblet at every centerpiece. On a three-step stage, a grand piano, a harp and a cello. In the middle, the dance floor: a wooden sun with the chalice at its center.

Low light, dark parquet, a green-and-gold rug with the chalice at its center. Two card tables, one for dice, a roulette the house calls the Wheel of Fortune, and a long bar of waxed wood with a wall of bottles behind it. In a corner, behind a gilded grille, the cashier.

The air changes at the door: warm, damp, smelling of salts. A long pool of blue mosaic reflects the light from the windows, the chalice and two dolphins rippling at the bottom. In a corner, a round bath bubbles on its own.

Past the portico, the noise of the square falls behind. A pebble path crosses the lawn to a round fountain, where an amber goblet the size of a child pours a thread of honey-colored water. There are red roses in bloom, and it is winter.

The staircase ends in a silent hall. The carpet is thick enough to swallow footsteps. A sofa, two armchairs and a tea table wait for no one in particular; beyond a glazed door, a balcony looks over the garden and the fountain.

The door opens on a salon someone half-emptied to make room for something else: seven gilded cages, each on a lit circle of runes, each holding something alive and the wrong color. In the middle, a table set for four, and a lord who does not rise.

From up here the whole city shows. The ochre tiles slope away on four sides and, in the middle of the north wing, the dome glows like an ember: through the glass, far below, you can see a round table with a map.

imagens_gm.leg: Light falls from the dome and everything turns the color of honey. On the floor, a compass rose of black marble and amber. At the center, a round table whose top is the entire city, with a piece for every debtor. Along the walls, blocks of amber on pedestals: inside one, a key; another, a ring; another, a quill. On a dais to the north, a mirror taller than a man in a gilded frame: it does not show the room, it shows a sky full of stars.
Dark shelves in three rows, with an aisle down the middle. At the far end, alone on a lectern under an amber light, a thick leather-bound book with gold corners.

Behind the amber slab, a room with no window. Black marble veined with gold, four torch brackets, and on the floor eight small stones in a circle that glow lilac when someone draws near. In the middle, nothing. Yet.

At the center of a mosaic floor, on a gilded stand, a sphere of dark amber the size of a barrel. Inside it, if you look too long, something moves: mouths. At a large table, facing the sphere, a man writes without stopping.

Adventure hooks

In through the musicLow level · 1–4

The Amber Quartet needs a fifth musician for the banquet. The four only talk while playing, because they know the goblets listen, and they want an outsider who can reach the third floor.

In through the doormanLow level · 1–4

Odo opens any door, including two that are on no plan, for whoever promises to return his grandfather's goblet: the one in the landing niche.

In through the debtMid level · 5–10

An indebted Club member offers his own invitation in exchange for making his line in the Ledger disappear.

The loose pane in the domeLow level · 1–4

A drunk tabaxi shouts in the square that the dome has a loose pane. It is true, and the house sent the Shields to remove him far too quickly.

The commander's signetMid level · 5–10

Veil-of-Smoke wants an amber block from the Pledge Chamber. Inside is the order with the forged signet that killed two Shields — and the manager's price to erase it is the new Commander.

Small package, great valueMid level · 5–10

A merchant staying here needs an escort to carry a small case to Kymal. Three other guests are very interested in that case.

The Mirror wakesHigh level · 11+

When the party enters the Amber Room, the Miracle Worker appears in the Mirror, in haste and not knowing whom he addresses: someone is taking the crystal that grows in Umbrasyl's blood beneath Gatshadow, and his three envoys never returned. At the end the glass shatters.

Headquarters of the regional Ranchers' Guild: pens, stables and a hall where plainscows and wagon contracts are traded.

The guild organizes the ranchers of the villages around Westruun, keeps the register of cattle brands and settles disputes over pasture and water. The meeting hall is rustic, with plainscow horns on the wall and a notice board always full of requests for help.

In their place: five-foot holes in the ground and traces of acid. Farmers and caravanners are frightened — the city's farming and trade are at risk. Jeremiah Sook, head of the guild, pays a hefty bounty for the culprits.

The red pins (where cattle vanished) form a straight line on the map: something underground is following a path.

Adventure hooks

They Can't Have Flown AwayLow levelOfficial hook

In one week, over four dozen plainscows vanished from the villages around Westruun. In their place: five-foot holes in the ground and traces of acid. Farmers and caravanners are frightened — the city's farming and trade are at risk. Jeremiah Sook, head of the guild, pays a hefty bounty for the culprits.

Brand thievesLow level · 1–4

Someone is rebranding stolen cattle and selling them at auction. Marta wants a name — and wants the Shields kept out of it.

Rumors (roll 1d6)

1The red pins mark where cattle vanished.True
2The notice board is the best source of work for beginners.True
3The Ravagers took all the missing cattle.False
4Huge holes were left where the cows were.True
5Marta Broadhorn doesn't trust the Shields.True
6The guild breeds flying plainscows.False

A party member wins too much at dice. On the way out, three polite men ask them to come back and “give the house a chance to win it back”.

locais.descricao:
Temple of the Dawnfather: a golden roof, a columned portico and a great sun disk in the forecourt that blazes at dawn.

The Dawnfather is widely revered on the plains, where the sun decides the harvest. Priests celebrate every dawn in the forecourt, and the faithful bring the year's first grain to be blessed. The temple also keeps a simple infirmary for those who cannot pay healers.
locais.narracao: The sun rises and the great golden disc in the forecourt ignites like a second morning. The faithful raise their hands together, and for a moment the whole city seems to fall silent.

imagens.leg: A temple with a golden roof and a columned portico, facing east. In the forecourt a golden disc larger than a man catches the first light of day and blazes. The faithful raise their hands together, and at the foot of the steps wait sacks of grain brought for blessing.

The All-Hammer's forge-temple: a low hall of dark stone, chimneys that never go out and a sacred anvil in the yard.

The city's dwarves and artisans gather here; the sacred forge has not gone out since the rebuilding, and every hammer stroke counts as a prayer. Priests bless tools, weapons and the cornerstones of new houses.
locais.narracao: The heat strikes your face before the door. The rhythm of the hammers is steady, almost music, and the floor hums along. Sparks rise up the chimneys like stars falling upward.

imagens.leg: Dark stone and chimneys that never go out. In the courtyard, a sacred anvil; around it priest-smiths hammer in one rhythm, like people praying. Sparks rise, the air shimmers with heat and everything is the orange of the forge.

The Changebringer's rotunda, with a copper dome and colorful banners — seat of the Changebringer's Court in the city.

The Changebringer is the goddess of change and freedom, and her faithful in Westruun helped reorganize the city after its liberation. The temple is open, noisy and full of assemblies where anyone can propose an idea — and be argued with.
locais.narracao: Colorful pennants snap in the wind above the copper dome. Inside, an assembly argues about something with such enthusiasm that no one notices who comes in.

The temple helps escaped slaves from Marquet and Kymal disappear into the city. The Clasp found out and wants “protection” money — or will sell the network out.

Freedom has a priceMid level · 5–10

Tamsa asks the party to escort a fugitive family through the Underwalk to the north exit. The Clasp and bounty hunters are on their trail.

Temple of the Storm Lord, with a sand training arena in front and a spire topped by a lightning rod.

The Storm Lord is the god of courage and fair battle, and many Shields of the Plain pray here before patrol. The arena in front hosts training and honor duels; anyone who wins three in a row earns a blessing from the high priest.
locais.narracao: On the arena sand two soldiers trade wooden blows while a priest with a braided beard counts hits aloud. Atop the spire, the lightning rod gleams against the sky.

npcs.ficha:
Spiral of Shadows, leader of the Clasp in Westruun

Starting attitudeHostile
Where to find{{local:vaca-de-sela}}
Sheet{{ficha:gholesh}}
“Everyone pays. The only question is in what.”

How to play

Laughs loud, eats with his mouth open, threatens in a joking voice.

Wants

Seize total control of the Clasp, secretly backed by the League of Miracles.

Knows / offers

Who owes what in the Mud and Residential Wards; smuggling routes.

Secret (GM only)

Betrays his own guild for the League — if the Clasp finds out, he dies.

Description

Leader of the Clasp in Westruun (Spiral of Shadows). His face is always hidden behind a leather ogre mask; his true appearance is a mystery. Crass and ambitious, he secretly allied with the League of Miracles to seize full control of the Clasp.

npcs.desc: A blue-skinned tiefling, Spiral of Blades of the Clasp: hairless face, curly hair, stubby horns and a childlike look that contrasts with a powerful build. Equally skilled with sword, axe and bow, she made her name in underground fighting rings.
npcs.ficha:
Spirali of Blades, the Clasp's muscle

Starting attitudeHostile
Where to find{{local:vaca-de-sela}}, {{local:sunkissed}}
Sheet{{ficha:melchior}}
“Pick your weapon. I'll pick the time.”

How to play

Speaks little, tests the reflexes of those around her, smiles only before a fight.

Wants

A fight worth having; respect in the ring.

Knows / offers

Where the underground fighting rings are and who fights in them.

Secret (GM only)

Works in an apron at the Sunkissed as “the new maid”. She is the one who opens the hatch behind the bar for the night cargo.

Description

A blue-skinned tiefling, Spiral of Blades of the Clasp: hairless face, curly hair, stubby horns and a childlike look that contrasts with a powerful build. Equally skilled with sword, axe and bow, she made her name in underground fighting rings.

npcs.desc: A halfling, Spiral of Secrets of the Clasp. His skeletal, unkempt look is a deliberate distraction from his cunning and sharp skill at manipulation.
npcs.ficha:
Spiral of Secrets of the Clasp

Starting attitudeWary
Where to find{{local:vaca-de-sela}}, {{local:sunkissed}}
Sheet{{ficha:busca}}
“Me? Just a poor wretch. But you dropped this… and this… and this.”

How to play

Hunched, whining voice, restless eyes. Pretends to be harmless.

Wants

Know everyone's secrets — and sell them at the right time.

Knows / offers

More than anyone in the Clasp: blackmail, lovers, debts.

Secret (GM only)

Works in an apron at the Sunkissed as “the new maid”. From there she watches who goes down to the cellar.

Description

A halfling, Spiral of Secrets of the Clasp. His skeletal, unkempt look is a deliberate distraction from his cunning and sharp skill at manipulation.

npcs.desc: A gnome cleric of the Lawbearer from Kymal, a wandering healer of the Golden Grin who lives on donations and travels door to door. Her friendly manner hides a constant gathering of whispers for the Grin.
npcs.ficha:
Wandering cleric of the Lawbearer and Golden Grin informant

Starting attitudeFriendly
Where to find{{local:temple-terrace}}
Sheet{{ficha:theona}}
“Let me see that wound. And tell me, dear, how did it happen?”

How to play

Motherly, hands always busy with balm, asks a lot and smiles more.

Wants

Hear everything whispered in the city, for the Golden Grin.

Knows / offers

Temple Ward gossip, who is sick, who is afraid.

Secret (GM only)

Every healing she performs becomes a file entry for the Grin.

Description

A gnome cleric of the Lawbearer from Kymal, a wandering healer of the Golden Grin who lives on donations and travels door to door. Her friendly manner hides a constant gathering of whispers for the Grin.

npcs.desc: A half-orc fiddler who leads Doctor Dranzel's Traveling Troupe. Jovial and careless on stage, he plays the fool on purpose: the perfect disguise for a spymaster of the Golden Grin.
npcs.ficha:
Street bard, tonic “doctor” and spymaster of the Golden Grin

Starting attitudeFriendly
Where to find{{local:public-forum}}
Sheet{{ficha:dranzel}}
“Ladies and gentlemen! The tonic that cures everything — even curiosity!”

How to play

Theatrical, arms wide, stage voice; turns suddenly serious when no one is looking.

Wants

Know before anyone else — and keep the Grin one step ahead of the Clasp.

Knows / offers

Everything that passes through the Public Forum, and much of what passes beneath it.

Secret (GM only)

The whole troupe is a spy network; the tonic is water and mint.

Description

A half-orc fiddler who leads Doctor Dranzel's Traveling Troupe. Jovial and careless on stage, he plays the fool on purpose: the perfect disguise for a spymaster of the Golden Grin.

npcs.desc: A middle-aged goliath, former leader of the Retrievers who overthrew Margrave Zimmerset. She has never lost a re-election. Direct and pragmatic, she distrusts easy answers to problems of debt and power and treats politics as an extension of the war she already fought.
npcs.ficha:
Lord Mayor of Westruun, former leader of the Retrievers

Starting attitudeIndifferent
Where to find{{local:lord-mayor}}
Sheet{{ficha:lysandra}}
“I already won one war in this city. Don't make me start another.”

How to play

A huge goliath, firm handshake, gets straight to the point. Hates evasion.

Wants

Pay off the debt to the League of Miracles without handing them the city.

Knows / offers

Who on the council votes with the League; where the Ravagers have been striking.

Secret (GM only)

Keeps the bought advisors in office on purpose, to watch the League.

Description

A middle-aged goliath, former leader of the Retrievers who overthrew Margrave Zimmerset. She has never lost a re-election. Direct and pragmatic, she distrusts easy answers to problems of debt and power and treats politics as an extension of the war she already fought.

npcs.desc: A tiefling blood mage, youngest of the League of Miracles: red eyes, paper-white skin and horns, red-and-white robes of the reclusive dwarven clans of the Alabaster Sierras. She led the rebuilding of the Market Ward. Fiercely dedicated and honorable — her peers fear she will denounce them if she learns the League's dirty truth.
npcs.ficha:
Blood mage of the League of Miracles; rebuilt the Market Ward

Starting attitudeIndifferent
Where to find{{local:exandrian-exchange}}, {{local:local-mwfd1fhv}}
Sheet{{ficha:kinnabari}}
“A deal is a deal. I keep mine. I expect the same.”

How to play

Impeccable posture, formal speech, never lies — prefers silence.

Wants

Prove her worth within the League.

Knows / offers

How much the city owes, to whom, and what was auctioned to pay it.

Secret (GM only)

She dines at the Chalice twice a week and finds it “overdone”. She has never passed the double doors of the Amber Room and never asked what the goblets do. Showing her the Amber Eye or the Ledger is the way to crack the League from within. Her adranach, Spark, is a horse-sized cub that waits in the garden by the fountain.

Description

A tiefling blood mage, youngest of the League of Miracles: red eyes, paper-white skin and horns, red-and-white robes of the reclusive dwarven clans of the Alabaster Sierras. She led the rebuilding of the Market Ward. Fiercely dedicated and honorable — her peers fear she will denounce them if she learns the League's dirty truth.

npcs.desc: A halfling paladin of the Platinum Dragon who calls the Platinum Dragon's Rest home. Wavy ash-red hair, a large scar across one side of her face, dented gold-and-silver plate and weapons far too big for her. Stubborn, impulsive and utterly devoted; fierce against enemies, caring toward allies.
npcs.ficha:
Halfling paladin of the Platinum Dragon

Starting attitudeFriendly
Where to find{{local:platinum-rest}}
Sheet{{ficha:kima}}
“Just tell me who the villain is. I'll bring the hammer.”

How to play

Impatient, taps her foot, laughs loud, eats chicken with her hands. Gentle with the weak.

Wants

Protect Westruun's poor and inspire younger adventurers.

Knows / offers

Who vanished from the temple's food line; stories of old heroes.

Secret (GM only)

Tends to act before thinking — and may wreck an investigation.

Description

A halfling paladin of the Platinum Dragon who calls the Platinum Dragon's Rest home. Wavy ash-red hair, a large scar across one side of her face, dented gold-and-silver plate and weapons far too big for her. Stubborn, impulsive and utterly devoted; fierce against enemies, caring toward allies.

npcs.desc: The temple guardian of the Platinum Dragon's Rest, who runs the services behind the scenes. Quiet, efficient, monastic; he treats pilgrims and nobles with the same formal courtesy.
npcs.ficha:
Guardian of the Platinum Dragon's Rest

Starting attitudeFriendly
Where to find{{local:platinum-rest}}
Sheet{{ficha:simar}}
“There's soup, a bed and silence. Choose what you need first.”

How to play

Polite, ceremonious, bows to everyone equally.

Wants

That the temple runs smoothly and no one else vanishes from the line.

Knows / offers

The name and story of nearly every poor soul who passes through the temple.

Secret (GM only)

Secretly notes who has vanished and has noticed a pattern.

Description

The temple guardian of the Platinum Dragon's Rest, who runs the services behind the scenes. Quiet, efficient, monastic; he treats pilgrims and nobles with the same formal courtesy.

npcs.desc: The grumpy half-orc barkeep of the Sunkissed Tavern and Inn. Stocky, bald on top, a chipped tusk, a broken nose and an apron stained by decades of spilled ale. He always has an ear open for valuable news — the classic barkeep who knows more than he lets on.
npcs.ficha:
Barkeep of the Sunkissed

Starting attitudeIndifferent
Where to find{{local:sunkissed}}
Sheet{{ficha:ulf}}
“Drink or leave. If you're going to talk, talk low.”

How to play

Grumbles, dries the same mug endlessly, never takes his eyes off the door.

Wants

Peace in his hall and good news to sell.

Knows / offers

Who arrived in town, who left in a hurry, what happened at the collapse to the south.

Secret (GM only)

Keeps letters from travelers who never came back.

Description

The grumpy half-orc barkeep of the Sunkissed Tavern and Inn. Stocky, bald on top, a chipped tusk, a broken nose and an apron stained by decades of spilled ale. He always has an ear open for valuable news — the classic barkeep who knows more than he lets on.

npcs.desc: A human baker in her late sixties who runs Softsky Bakery, now with her son Simon. Her tight braid is almost all white, with one stubborn red strand. Reserved and tired but firm. Years ago, Simon was taken by the Dread Emperor and rescued by Vox Machina; any mention of a strange child makes her panic.
npcs.ficha:
Baker, owner of Softsky Bakery

Starting attitudeWary
Where to find{{local:softsky}}
Sheet{{ficha:elowen}}
“The bread is good. That should be enough, shouldn't it?”

How to play

Tired, floury hands, wary of strangers who ask about her son.

Wants

Keep the bakery open and her son safe.

Knows / offers

Everything said on her street before dawn.

Secret (GM only)

Is behind on rent and has been threatened by the landlord.

Description

A human baker in her late sixties who runs Softsky Bakery, now with her son Simon. Her tight braid is almost all white, with one stubborn red strand. Reserved and tired but firm. Years ago, Simon was taken by the Dread Emperor and rescued by Vox Machina; any mention of a strange child makes her panic.

npcs.desc: Elowen's son, a tall, quiet man in his mid-thirties with thinning red hair and baker's hands. He always wears a scarf around his neck. Kind and protective; as a child he was one of the Dread Emperor's captives.
npcs.ficha:
Elowen's son, the bakery's helper

Starting attitudeFriendly
Where to find{{local:softsky}}
Sheet{{ficha:simon}}
“Are you adventurers? Really? Have you killed a dragon?”

How to play

Eager, talks fast, protects his mother without being asked.

Wants

Live an adventure — and help his mother pay the bills.

Knows / offers

Shortcuts across the Residential Ward's rooftops.

Secret (GM only)

Sneaks out to the rooftops at night; has seen something tall walking the street.

Description

Elowen's son, a tall, quiet man in his mid-thirties with thinning red hair and baker's hands. He always wears a scarf around his neck. Kind and protective; as a child he was one of the Dread Emperor's captives.

npcs.desc: A reclusive archmage who lives in Greystone Tower. Cautious and observant, he has a history of testing adventurers before trusting them. He keeps the tower isolated for good reasons, not mere eccentricity.
npcs.ficha:
Realmseer, archmage of Greystone Tower

Starting attitudeWary
Where to find{{local:greystone-tower}}
Sheet{{ficha:eskil}}
“If you made it this far, you passed the first test. Don't get excited.”

How to play

Speaks in riddles, watches before acting, tests everyone.

Wants

Keep imprisoned whatever he holds inside the tower.

Knows / offers

Much about ancient magic and dangers the city can't imagine.

Secret (GM only)

He is running out of strength; he can't hold on alone much longer.

Description

A reclusive archmage who lives in Greystone Tower. Cautious and observant, he has a history of testing adventurers before trusting them. He keeps the tower isolated for good reasons, not mere eccentricity.

npcs.desc: Realmseer Ryndarien's assistant: thin, disheveled, crooked spectacles mended with copper wire, sleeves dusted with magical residue of changing colors. Anxious but competent enough to survive years beside an eccentric archmage. He is the one who writes for help when his master vanishes.
npcs.ficha:
The Realmseer's assistant

Starting attitudeFriendly
Where to find{{local:greystone-tower}}
Sheet{{ficha:jekt}}
“Please, please — he'll be furious if I ask for help, but he'll be dead if I don't.”

How to play

Nervous, wrings his hands, talks too much, but knows exactly what he's doing.

Wants

Get his master out of the tower alive.

Knows / offers

How the tower works from outside — and some secrets from within.

Secret (GM only)

Knows what his master is holding and is afraid to say.

Description

Realmseer Ryndarien's assistant: thin, disheveled, crooked spectacles mended with copper wire, sleeves dusted with magical residue of changing colors. Anxious but competent enough to survive years beside an eccentric archmage. He is the one who writes for help when his master vanishes.

npcs.desc: Head of the regional Ranchers' Guild: sturdy, sun-weathered, a battered wide-brimmed hat and a thick grey mustache he tugs when worried — which lately is always. Direct and practical, genuinely concerned for the farmers he represents.
npcs.ficha:
Leading rancher in the Ranchers' Guild

Starting attitudeFriendly
Where to find{{local:local-mwfd5a0q}}
Sheet{{ficha:sook}}
“Forty cows don't vanish into thin air. Someone — or something — took them.”

How to play

Practical, hat in hand, counts everything in head of cattle.

Wants

Find what is taking the cattle before the villages go broke.

Knows / offers

Where each cow vanished; the holes left in the ground.

Secret (GM only)

Pays the reward out of his own pocket because the guild is broke.

Description

Head of the regional Ranchers' Guild: sturdy, sun-weathered, a battered wide-brimmed hat and a thick grey mustache he tugs when worried — which lately is always. Direct and practical, genuinely concerned for the farmers he represents.

npcs.desc: High priest of the First Bastion. Grave and responsible, with fresh shadows under his eyes; he feels the weight of every investigator lost in the pit beneath his own temple.
npcs.ficha:
High Priest of the First Bastion

Starting attitudeIndifferent
Where to find{{local:first-bastion}}
Sheet{{ficha:helmdoff}}
“Law is the stone a city stands on. And my stone is cracking.”

How to play

Grave, pulpit voice, hands clasped behind his back, carries the weight of guilt.

Wants

Save those who fell beneath the temple and understand what opened below.

Knows / offers

The history of the occupation and the shelters beneath the temple.

Secret (GM only)

He sent the first investigators and feels responsible for their deaths.

Description

High priest of the First Bastion. Grave and responsible, with fresh shadows under his eyes; he feels the weight of every investigator lost in the pit beneath his own temple.

npcs.desc: One of the tiefling twin mages who run the dream-reading stall, each with a single horn. Lavender-grey skin, silver hair shaved on one side, eyes without whites. Charming and rehearsed — perhaps too rehearsed.
npcs.ficha:
Dream reader (half of the stall)

Starting attitudeWary
Where to find{{local:dream-stall}}
Sheet{{ficha:nyx}}
“Your dream smells of wet earth. Am I right?”

How to play

Low voice, distant gaze, holds the client's hand while they speak.

Wants

Make money — and make the nightmares stop.

Knows / offers

What the figure in all the nightmares looks like.

Secret (GM only)

Has a real, faint gift for seeing dreams — and is terrified by what she saw.

Description

One of the tiefling twin mages who run the dream-reading stall, each with a single horn. Lavender-grey skin, silver hair shaved on one side, eyes without whites. Charming and rehearsed — perhaps too rehearsed.

npcs.desc: Nyx's twin: shorter, rust-colored skin, a single straight horn in the middle of the forehead, a cloak full of little vials of sleep dust. The two finish each other's sentences.
npcs.ficha:
Dream interpreter (the other half of the stall)

Starting attitudeWary
Where to find{{local:dream-stall}}
Sheet{{ficha:vryll}}
“That means change. Or danger. Five silver, please.”

How to play

Quick patter, salesman's smile, protects his sister fiercely.

Wants

Keep the business running and his sister out of trouble.

Knows / offers

Who the clients are and which neighborhoods the nightmares come from.

Secret (GM only)

Makes up the interpretations — but writes down everything his sister really sees.

Description

Nyx's twin: shorter, rust-colored skin, a single straight horn in the middle of the forehead, a cloak full of little vials of sleep dust. The two finish each other's sentences.

npcs.desc: Headmistress of Westhall Academy and a blood descendant of the heroic wizard Atz Yuminor. She supports the Scions of Yuminor, the observatory's order of diviners. (No physical description in the source — to be created.)
npcs.ficha:
Headmistress of Westhall Academy, descendant of Atz Yuminor

Starting attitudeFriendly
Where to find{{local:westhall-academy}}, {{local:yuminor-observatory}}
Sheet{{ficha:estella}}
“Talent is common. Discipline is rare. Which did you bring?”

How to play

Corrects others' grammar, writes everything down, smiles sincerely only at students.

Wants

Scholarships for all — and for the observatory to stay out of trouble.

Knows / offers

Who's who among the city's scholars; what the diviners have been seeing.

Secret (GM only)

Knows about the diviners' marked date and ordered its records burned.

Description

Appearance. A human in her early fifties, grey hair in a firm bun, round spectacles and midnight-blue robes embroidered with constellations. Always carries a leather clipboard.

Personality. Demanding and generous in equal measure: she believes any child from the plains can be a genius if given a chance. Hates it when people speak of her famous ancestor as if that explained her merit.

Headmistress of Westhall Academy and a blood descendant of the heroic wizard Atz Yuminor. She supports the Scions of Yuminor, the observatory's order of diviners. (No physical description in the source — to be created.)

npcs.desc: The statue of Palest Westruun on horseback in the Opal Ward square, blessed by the First Bastion's high priest. It awakens when the whole city is threatened: a stone golem with 60 ft. speed, Int and Cha 18 (+4), speaking Common. Dour, regal and single-minded about protecting its people.
npcs.ficha:
Golem-statue of Palest Westruun, guardian of the city

Starting attitudeIndifferent
Where to find{{local:public-forum}}
Sheet{{ficha:reinegro}}
“Westruun endures.”

How to play

A voice from the ground; turns its head slowly; never negotiates.

Wants

That the city survive.

Knows / offers

Vaguely remembers the life of Palest, the founder.

Secret (GM only)

Can be tricked into waking against a single target, if someone makes the city seem in danger.

Description

Appearance. A dark stone rider on a rearing horse, three times a man's height. When it wakes, cracks glow amber across its body and the stone grinds like thunder.

Personality. Dour, regal and single-minded. Speaks little, in old-fashioned phrases, and cares only for the safety of the whole city — never for one person alone.

The statue of Palest Westruun on horseback in the Opal Ward square, blessed by the First Bastion's high priest. It awakens when the whole city is threatened: a stone golem with 60 ft. speed, Int and Cha 18 (+4), speaking Common. Dour, regal and single-minded about protecting its people.

npcs.desc: A sadistic oni that steals children and sows nightmares across the city (hook The Stuff of Nightmares). A master of disguise who knows how to erase its tracks.
npcs.ficha:
An oni who steals children and sows nightmares

Starting attitudeHostile
Where to find{{local:oni-cavern}}
Sheet{{ficha:oni}}
“Sleep, little one. I'll watch the door.”

How to play

A sweet voice that suddenly deepens; low laughter; never fights where it can't flee.

Wants

Fear — from dreams and from children.

Knows / offers

Who in the city fears what most.

Secret (GM only)

While the nightmares last, it grows stronger. Ending them weakens it.

Description

Appearance. In true form, a tall blue-grey ogre with curved horns, beastly teeth and yellow eyes that glow in the dark. In the city, it wears the face of someone kind and familiar.

Personality. Sadistic, patient and vain. It likes to be feared in dreams before it is ever seen awake.

A sadistic oni that steals children and sows nightmares across the city (hook The Stuff of Nightmares). A master of disguise who knows how to erase its tracks.

npcs.desc: A city guard soldier: reinforced leather and a blue-grey surcoat with the crest of Westruun. There are about 1,200 of them, stretched far too thin.
npcs.ficha:
Shield of the Plain soldier (city guard)

Starting attitudeIndifferent
Where to find{{local:lord-mayor}}
Sheet{{ficha:escudo}}
“Move along. And sheathe that sword before I have to fill out paperwork.”

How to play

Leans on the spear, yawns, but snaps alert the moment someone shouts.

Wants

Finish the shift without trouble.

Knows / offers

Barracks rumors and where fights broke out this week.

Secret (GM only)

Some take Clasp coin to look the other way.

Description

Appearance. Studded leather and mail, a blue-grey surcoat bearing Westruun's white horse, spear and round shield. Boots always muddy from the plains.

Personality. Tired, underpaid and proud. Nearly all lost someone in the war; they respect those who help the city and loathe adventurers who cause trouble.

A city guard soldier: reinforced leather and a blue-grey surcoat with the crest of Westruun. There are about 1,200 of them, stretched far too thin.

npcs.desc: A veteran officer of the Shields of the Plain, tired of too many patrols and too few soldiers.
npcs.ficha:
Veteran captain of the Shields of the Plain

Starting attitudeWary
Where to find{{local:lord-mayor}}
Sheet{{ficha:capitao}}
“I have thirty soldiers for three villages. You have five minutes.”

How to play

Speaks in orders, studies maps while talking, accepts no excuses.

Wants

More people, more weapons and fewer adventurers making a mess.

Knows / offers

Where the Ravagers struck; who's smuggling through the gates.

Secret (GM only)

Knows which guards take bribes — and is waiting to catch them all at once.

Description

Appearance. A woman with short grey hair, a scar on her chin, worn plate armor and a blue cloak bearing the white horse. A shield painted with the city crest.

Personality. Curt, fair and exhausted. Too few soldiers, too many problems; she hires adventurers without liking it.

A veteran officer of the Shields of the Plain, tired of too many patrols and too few soldiers.

npcs.desc: A Clasp thief, fence or enforcer. The guild's sign is tattooed between the shoulder blades.
npcs.ficha:
Clasp agent (thief, fence or collector)

Starting attitudeHostile
Where to find{{local:vaca-de-sela}}, {{local:clasp-manhole}}
Sheet{{ficha:fivela}}
“Nice purse. It'd be a shame if it… disappeared.”

How to play

Crooked smile, flips a coin hand to hand, never turns their back to the door.

Wants

Make this week's quota.

Knows / offers

An old knock, a hideout, the name of their superior.

Secret (GM only)

Gives up information for protection — if they fear the party more than the guild.

Description

Appearance. Plain dark clothes, a hood, several hidden knives. The guild's symbol — a buckle — tattooed between the shoulder blades.

Personality. Loyal to the guild out of fear and money. Prefers threats to fighting, and fleeing to dying.

A Clasp thief, fence or enforcer. The guild's sign is tattooed between the shoulder blades.

npcs.desc:
Appearance. A slender figure with long white hair, all-white clothes with silver embroidery, a lute on the back and a smooth white mask never removed.

Personality. Dramatic, generous to students, cruel to critics. Always speaks as if on stage.
npcs.ficha:
Masked founder of the College of the Savvy

Starting attitudeFriendly
Where to find{{local:college-savvy}}, {{local:trickfoot-park}}
Sheet{{ficha:duque-branco}}
“Every city is a theater. Westruun just forgot it's on stage.”

How to play

Wide gestures, rhymes by accident, never answers plainly if a song will do.

Wants

That art be free — and the League of Miracles be ridiculed.

Knows / offers

Noble and backstage gossip; who sponsors whom.

Secret (GM only)

It is a title worn by three teachers who take turns with the mask.

Description

Appearance. A slender figure with long white hair, all-white clothes with silver embroidery, a lute on the back and a smooth white mask never removed.

Personality. Dramatic, generous to students, cruel to critics. Always speaks as if on stage.

npcs.desc:
Appearance. A red-haired half-elf with a long braid, spectacles, a patched green cloak full of pockets; an orb of light always floats near her hand.

Personality. Patient as stone, firm as a wall. She has taken fire, ice and lightning from students and never raised her voice.
npcs.ficha:
Head teacher of the Ljunian School for the Gifted

Starting attitudeFriendly
Where to find{{local:ljunian}}
Sheet{{ficha:odalys}}
“Breathe. Count to ten. Now let the fire go — slowly, into the bucket.”

How to play

Speaks slowly and softly, touches nervous shoulders, never shows fear.

Wants

Find the runaway student before he hurts someone — or gets hurt.

Knows / offers

Much about wild magic and gifted children in the plains villages.

Secret (GM only)

Suspects one of her students is not what they seem.

Description

Appearance. A red-haired half-elf with a long braid, spectacles, a patched green cloak full of pockets; an orb of light always floats near her hand.

Personality. Patient as stone, firm as a wall. She has taken fire, ice and lightning from students and never raised her voice.

npcs.desc:
Appearance. A tall, thin old man with a white moustache, red frock coat, a wide-brimmed feathered hat and a gold-headed cane.

Personality. Proud, snobbish, but loyal to family. Treats money as proof of character.
npcs.ficha:
Head of the Barkley family, rich from cattle and wagons

Starting attitudeIndifferent
Where to find{{local:barkley-manor}}
Sheet{{ficha:ordo-barkley}}
“The Barkleys don't ask for favors. We buy them.”

How to play

Taps his cane to end conversations; never shakes hands with strangers.

Wants

That the wagon thefts stop and the family name stays clean.

Knows / offers

Contracts, wagon routes and the secrets of the city's other rich.

Secret (GM only)

Doesn't know his own son is selling his routes to the Clasp.

Description

Appearance. A tall, thin old man with a white moustache, red frock coat, a wide-brimmed feathered hat and a gold-headed cane.

Personality. Proud, snobbish, but loyal to family. Treats money as proof of character.

npcs.desc:
Appearance. A handsome young man with messy dark hair, an expensive green coat already worn, and the dark circles of someone who doesn't sleep.

Personality. Charming, spoiled and terrified. Lies by reflex and regrets it immediately.
npcs.ficha:
The youngest Barkley, in debt to the Clasp

Starting attitudeWary

paginas.html:
Westruun is the heart of Tal'Dorei, a crossroads of cultures on the Silvercut Roadway that welcomes adventurers, traders and vagabonds. Despite its name it lies more east than west: it was named after Palest Westruun, the trader and philosopher who founded it. It suffered under Kevdak's Herd of Storms and the acid of Umbrasyl, yet was one of the first cities to recover from the Chroma Conclave — deep in debt to the League of Miracles. Population about 52,000.

Lord Mayor Lysandra Kallos, a middle-aged goliath and former leader of the Retrievers, has never lost an election. About 1,200 Shields of the Plain guard the walls and outlying villages, stretched too thin to deal with the Ravagers on the plains, so mercenaries and adventurers always find bloody work here.

Long before the walls come into view you feel the wind — constant, smelling of tilled earth and forge smoke. Farms stretch for miles up to the great stone walls, patched here and there with paler new stone. Behind, Gatshadow cuts the sky like a blade, its twin peaks wrapped in grey mist. On the road, merchant wagons jostle with pilgrims and dusty adventurers. Someone shouts a price; someone shouts back, laughing. Westruun never sleeps — it haggles.
